code.originalText: Midpoint of chemotherapy: CA-125, blood counts, neuropathy, and menopausal symptoms

text.paragraph: Review at the midpoint of chemotherapy, on the day of cycle 4. [S]

Ms. Radner returns on the day of her fourth cycle of carboplatin and paclitaxel. Cycles 2 and 3 were given on schedule. The cold she had a week after cycle 2 cleared in five days without a fever. Nausea lasts a day or two after each cycle and is controlled with ondansetron, which she uses two or three times per cycle. For about two weeks she has had tingling in her toes and fingertips that does not stop her buttoning clothes, walking, or writing. Her hair has fallen out and she wears a scarf. Hot flashes continue. She goes to her support group every other week. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1986-07-14; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 55.9 kg; blood pressure 110/70, pulse 80
Soft, non-tender; no fluid or mass
Pinprick slightly reduced over the toes; vibration sense and ankle reflexes present; strength normal; steady gait

Persistent bloating with tightness of her clothes, feeling full after a few bites, a dull lower abdominal and pelvic ache, and passing urine more often, on most days for about four weeks, in a woman of 39: the ovarian cancer symptom index is positive. Examination: a distended abdomen with shifting dullness and a firm, fixed, irregular mass in the right adnexa. Suspected ovarian cancer; transvaginal ultrasound, CT, CA-125 and gynecologic oncology review booked within the week
S — Synthetic presenting problem linked to her documented abdominal symptoms; superseded by the diagnosis at the gynecologic oncology consultation.

High-grade serous carcinoma of both ovaries (Mullerian origin), diagnosed by image-guided omental core biopsy (PAX8 and WT1 positive, p53 aberrant), with bilateral adnexal masses, ascites, omental and diaphragmatic disease on CT: clinical FIGO stage IIIC; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented ovarian cancer
S — Synthetic histology and stage; the documented diagnosis was stage IV ovarian cancer (D).
Peritoneal and omental metastases of the ovarian cancer, with ascites
S — Synthetic extent of disease on CT and biopsy.
Family history of ovarian cancer in three relatives (her grandmother, an aunt, and a cousin) in a woman of Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry; no genetic testing in the family is known
S — Synthetic coding of her documented family history; the basis for genetic counseling.

Acute viral upper respiratory infection on day 8 of the second chemotherapy cycle: two days of sore throat, runny nose and a dry cough, without fever; rapid influenza and COVID-19 tests negative; resolved
S — Synthetic acute infection; not a historical claim.
Symptomatic surgical menopause after bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy at 39: hot flashes and night sweats
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic operation.
Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy from paclitaxel: tingling in the toes and fingertips, grade 1 (sensory only, no effect on daily activities)
S — Synthetic common effect of paclitaxel.

list.item:
High-grade serous ovarian cancer, stage IIIC, on chemotherapy (C56.3). Responding: CA-125 is normal at 21 U/mL, from 188. Counts allow cycle 4: neutrophils 1.9, platelets 188; hemoglobin 10.3 g/dL, mild anemia from chemotherapy without symptoms. Kidney and liver function are normal. Magnesium is at the lower limit (1.7 mg/dL) after three cycles of carboplatin. [S]
Cycle 4 today at full dose.
Magnesium-rich foods; recheck before each remaining cycle.
CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis after cycle 6.

Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, grade 1 (G62.0). Grade 1 sensory neuropathy from paclitaxel, without functional effect. No medicine has been shown to prevent it; the dose is reduced if symptoms begin to interfere with daily activities (grade 2) or become painful. [S]
Continue paclitaxel at full dose with a check before each cycle.
Report trouble with buttons, writing, or balance, or burning pain.
Duloxetine if it becomes painful.

Symptomatic surgical menopause (E89.41). Hot flashes continue and she is coping with non-hormonal measures. [S]
Discuss hormone therapy at the end of treatment.

Acute viral upper respiratory infection (J06.9). Resolved without fever. [S]
No further action.
